messages.text: Quick one: a member just asked to withdraw $9,500 cash from checking. Our drawer limit is $5,000 per teller before we need vault approval, right? Don't want to get this wrong.
Yep, $5,000 at the window without a supervisor override. Anything above that needs the vault cash order form and a manager sign-off. Also give the member a heads-up that it may take a few minutes.
And anything over $10,000 triggers the CTR, so $9,500 is under, but be careful if they've already taken cash out today. Check the day's aggregate in CoreBanking before you hand it over.
Good call, Nichole. Looked at the aggregate and there was nothing earlier today on {{ACCOUNT_NUMBER:a_00099}}. Member says it's for a car purchase from a private seller.
Fair. Just do the usual conversation about why they're carrying that much cash and note it in MemberCRM. A cashier's check might be safer for them anyway. Offer it if they're open to it.
Offered. They're fine with a cashier's check for most of it and $1,500 cash. Thanks both, that saves a trip to the vault.
Heads up for the floor: my drawer was over the $15,000 max after the morning deposits. I'm doing a cash-out to the vault at 1:45 if anyone needs me to hold off on large withdrawals until then.
Thanks Jonathan. Remember the buy-back needs two people for the count and both initials on the slip. Auditors flagged a missing initial last quarter.
Got it. Catherine, can you be my second count at 1:45?
Sure, I'll be there. Just finishing with {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0044}} first.

Reminder: {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0036}} called asking if we can raise their daily cash withdrawal limit for next week. I told them limits are set by Compliance and Paul, so I'll send the request there. Please don't promise anything at the window.
Agreed. {{CLIENT_NAME:c_0036}} is in my book, so loop me in and I'll follow up with them once Paul and Wesley respond.
